They publish NO per-plant control equipment, emissions or measurements: they are occupational-safety management-system scorecards, one aggregate points total per company. category: Annual temporal class summarises a mixed monthly profile
dataset: outputs/pakemis_source_streams.csv temporal_class against outputs/national_monthly_2024.csv temporal_method
unblocks: the T-class mass shares in outputs/temporal_profile.csv, and any monthly evidence grading
note: MEASURED, NOT SUSPECTED: 81 of 190 source streams carry a monthly profile that mixes temporal classes across the twelve months, and the annual row reports the modal month rather than the weakest. Two published consequences: the stream registry records ZERO T1 streams while the monthly product emits 75 T1 rows, and the agricultural soils streams read T2 annually while three of their months are T3. Neither figure is wrong - they answer different questions - but nothing said so, and a reader comparing them finds a contradiction. The correct rule is that a stream is only as resolved as its worst month, so the annual class should be the FLOOR of its months; applying it moves the national T-class mass shares (T1 0.94 / T2 12.46 / T3 14.97 / T4 71.62 percent) and therefore belongs to the 108-month build, not to a release freeze.

category: Domestic wastewater - effluent N2O discharge pathway
dataset: the fraction of generated wastewater nitrogen actually discharged to an aquatic environment, and the nitrogen removed as sludge, by sanitation route
holder: WHO/UNICEF JMP; provincial WASA utilities; PCRWR
unblocks: a pathway-split effluent N2O estimate under the 2019 Refinement
note: THE DENOMINATOR IS WIDER THAN THE FACTOR. ww_ef_effluent is 0.005 kg N2O-N per kg N, which IPCC defines for nitrogen DISCHARGED TO AN AQUATIC ENVIRONMENT, and wastewater.n2o_gg applies it to all nitrogen the population generates - people x protein x F_NPR x F_NON-CON x F_IND-COM - with no discharge-pathway split and no N_SLUDGE subtraction, where IPCC 2006 Eq 6.9 has N_EFFLUENT = N_total - N_sludge. Nitrogen in routes that do not reach water (pit latrines, septic to ground, land application) is therefore charged the aquatic factor. The sanitation panel the sector already uses for methane (the JMP stratification behind the MCF) is the natural place a split would come from, so this is a reconciliation rather than an acquisition. The 2019 Refinement separates the two pathways explicitly - Eq 6.7 for treatment plants with pathway-specific factors and Eq 6.8 for effluent discharged to aquatic environments - and resolving this means choosing which of those this category is estimating. Direction of the bias is UP on effluent N2O, by the share of nitrogen that never reaches water; the magnitude is unquantified because that share is exactly what is missing. Opened 2026-10-05 from the biomass lane's parameter trace.
